behaviors.execution_owner: Raft main loop, campaign RPC workers
behaviors.protocol_context: Current term and latest configuration; campaign-local reply channel
behaviors.trigger: Follower contact expiry or TimeoutNow; candidate election retries
implementation_guards: Only latest-configuration voters are solicited. Normal follower timeout requires local voting eligibility. Pre-vote precedes term increment unless disabled or leadership transfer.

Vote handlers check known leader, candidate configuration membership, terms, prior persisted vote, and lexicographic last-log term/index freshness. A newer-term request may cause step-down before rejection as nonvoter.
writes: Term, role, known leader, last-contact, campaign tally
durable_effects: Current term stored before publishing; vote term then candidate bytes stored before granting
external_effects: A campaign majority changes role to Leader; higher-term vote reply changes to Follower
async_boundaries: One buffered reply channel per campaign; old replies do not enter a later campaign tally

cross_activity_effects.A1: Elects owner of a fresh commitment context using persisted log freshness
cross_activity_effects.A6: Reads durable vote and last log/snapshot history

unknowns: Failure semantics between the two vote persistence writes remain unexamined.

writes: Fresh commitment startIndex, inflight list, replication map, verification map, stepDown channel

async_boundaries: Each replicator retains this tenure commitment pointer and stepDown channel; old workers can finish against detached state

cross_activity_effects.A1: New commitment requires a current-term entry before advancing old prefix
cross_activity_effects.A7: Leadership loss does not certify that a previously submitted write was never committed

async_boundaries: Pipeline decoding and heartbeat run separately; replication fallback and commit timeout provide later attempts

cross_activity_effects.A2: A newer response term signals this tenure to step down
cross_activity_effects.A3: Snapshot restores participation when log replay cannot reach peer

implementation_guards: Reject older term or mismatching predecessor; skip same-term duplicate entries; delete conflicting suffix then store new entries
writes: Role/term/known leader, log suffix, latest/committed configuration, commitIndex and queued lastApplied
durable_effects: Replacement logs persist before successful response
external_effects: With positive newer LeaderCommitIndex, queues up to min(LeaderCommitIndex, local last index); successful response refreshes contact. Empty heartbeat producer carries zero commit index.

implementation_guards: Leader admits changes only after prior latest configuration and current-term no-op are committed. nextConfiguration checks prevIndex, unique nonempty IDs/addresses and at least one voter.

external_effects: AddVoter grants Voter directly; replication includes Nonvoters too. A following configuration entry implies preceding configuration committed on follower.

behaviors.execution_owner: Main-loop verifyLeader and asynchronous followerReplication notifications
behaviors.protocol_context: One verifyFuture attached to current tenure replicators
behaviors.trigger: Public VerifyLeader admitted on verifyCh; response-triggered vote notification
implementation_guards: Threshold is latest voter count / 2 + 1; initial self vote is one. vote lock permits only one terminal notification per future.
writes: Future votes and quorumSize; each replicator notify set
external_effects: verifyLeader registers the future with every replicator and requests immediate heartbeats. notifyAll forwards success booleans without identity/suffrage; leader loop returns nil once votes reach threshold or steps down on early negative notification.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Aggregates support for authority verification using voter-derived threshold
cross_activity_effects.A7: Successful public verification is intended to prevent stale reads after leadership loss

existing_protections: Leader lease separately counts only Voter contact and eventually steps down on insufficient contact. Main-loop tenure exit fails tracked verification futures.
unknowns: Can a reachable Nonvoter success complete VerifyLeader while the old leader has lost voter-majority contact and another leader exists, before lease step-down?
Configuration changes concurrent with a pending verification may reinterpret threshold/support; this is a separate unresolved context.

facts.meaning: Per-server greatest acknowledged matching log index retained by a particular leader commitment object for IDs currently admitted as voters.
facts.validity_context: One leader tenure; setConfiguration changes the eligible ID map and retains indexes for retained voters.
facts.durability: Volatile tracker; underlying log/snapshot persistence is reported by successful producer paths.
facts.recovery: Recreated with zero matches and a new startIndex for each tenure.

facts.meaning: Local index recorded as committed by either leader majority aggregation or follower consumption of a leader commit bound; this is distinct from completed FSM execution.
facts.validity_context: Leader tenure aggregation or follower append history; correctness of each producer bound is not assumed.
facts.durability: Volatile index; durable logs/snapshots carry recoverable history.
facts.recovery: Snapshot recovers applied boundary; subsequent leader/follower commit processing reconstructs later advancement.
unknowns: Follower local-last-index bound may exceed entries matched by one bounded request.

facts.meaning: A verifyFuture records one initial self vote plus successful notifications until its voter-derived numerical quorum threshold or an early negative terminal notification is reached; the tally itself carries no peer identity or suffrage.
facts.validity_context: One verification request registered in a leader tenure; threshold sampled from latest voter count at registration.
facts.durability: Volatile; not a durable election or log commitment.
facts.recovery: No replay; tenure exit responds ErrLeadershipLost to pending tracked requests.
unknowns: Whether nonvoter support can make public verification falsely succeed after authority loss under a legal partition.

surfaces.reason: Can a legal bounded AppendEntries consume an unmatched local suffix before later batches replace it?
Which later actions consume stale last-log cache after truncation succeeds but replacement write fails, under which applicable storage fault contract?
Does nonvoter notification satisfy a voter quorum threshold after voter-majority authority is lost?

formation.explanation: Leader dispatch assigns term/index and persists locally, then self-matches and wakes per-peer replication. Replicators backtrack on mismatch, send bounded log batches or snapshots, and report successful progress into the tenure commitment object. Only eligible voter matches count; the majority boundary must reach the first index of this term. Main loop receives commit notification, updates configuration commitment, and queues entries. Followers accept matching predecessors, reconcile suffixes and use leader commit metadata to queue local history. FSM callbacks and futures complete asynchronously after queuing.

context.explanation: Follower contact timeout starts campaigns only with local voter eligibility; optional pre-vote precedes persisted term/vote advancement. Vote handling checks membership, known leader, term, prior vote and last-log freshness. Campaign-local replies form the authority majority. New leadership allocates fresh support state and a no-op. Higher terms, insufficient voter lease contact or removal cause loss; transfer catches a target up and sends TimeoutNow, temporarily suppressing new writes. Tenure exit detaches old support state and fails pending client/verification work.

connection.explanation: Log freshness and durable votes constrain authority acquisition. New tenure match accounting starts afresh, but retained log history may advance only when a current-term entry gains majority support. Latest configuration governs voter eligibility; stable-configuration admission waits for prior commitment and the tenure no-op, while truncation and snapshots reconstruct configuration context. Old replication replies retain the old commitment pointer, not the new tenure tracker. Already queued committed FSM work is separate from inflight work failed at step-down; leadership loss is an ambiguous client outcome. Startup reconstructs term, log/snapshot and membership before beginning follower work. Verification separately aggregates replication notifications; its numerical tally does not itself establish voting eligibility, which is the selected unresolved premise.

core_overview.rationale: Representative formation and context transitions are traced through producers, aggregators, consumers, persistence, recovery and completion. Local anomalies and detailed concurrency/fault variants remain open, without asserting exhaustive coverage.
